headline: Siakam, Zubac power the Pacers to a 114-101 win over the Wizards
text: INDIANAPOLIS -- — Pascal Siakam scored 28 points and Ivica Zubac finished with 20 points and 12 rebounds as the Indiana Pacers beat the Washington Wizards 114-101 on Wednesday night. Siakam was 7 of 17 from the field and converted all 12 of his chances at the line. Andrew Nembhard added 17 points and 10 assists and Kelly Oubre Jr . scored all 14 of his points in the first half for Indiana. Kyshawn George scored 25 points and Anthony Davis had 21 points and 13 rebounds for the Wizards, who lost their fifth straight. Trae Young scored 12 of his 15 points in the second half and Tre Johnson added 15 points off the bench for the Wizards. Indiana, which snapped a two-game skid, went on a 14-0 run to open the fourth quarter for a 91-77 lead. The Pacers had led 69-59 with 6:24 left in the quarter before the Wizards responded with an 18-8 outburst to close the quarter. The Wizards took their largest lead of the game at 41-33 midway through the second quarter before the Pacers closed the half with a 22-9 run for a 55-50 halftime lead. Indiana shot 46% while holding the Wizards to 39% in the opening half. For the game, the Pacers shot 47%, while the Wizards finished at 41%. Pacers coach Rick Carlisle said Tyrese Haliburton 's left hamstring strain is progressing, but added it is reasonable that he might have a status update in 10 days. Haliburton has missed eight consecutive games. Up next Wizards: Host Detroit on Thursday. Pacers: Host New York on Friday.

headline: James Harden scores a season-high 32 points as the Cavaliers beat the Knicks 115-107
text: NEW YORK -- — James Harden scored a season-high 32 points, more than double his average during a tough start to 2026-27, and the Cleveland Cavaliers beat the New York Knicks 115-107 on Wednesday night. Donovan Mitchell added 23 for the Cavaliers in their first trip to Madison Square Garden since the Eastern Conference finals, when the Knicks erased a 22-point deficit in the fourth quarter of Game 1 to win in overtime, then took Game 2 en route to a four-game sweep. This time the Cavaliers were better down the stretch, with Harden hitting a go-ahead 3-pointer to snap a 101-all tie with 4:21 remaining. The three-time NBA scoring champion came in averaging 15.3 points for the season and shooting just 36.4% from the floor. Jalen Brunson scored 27 for the Knicks, who had their four-game winning streak snapped. Karl-Anthony Towns had 21 points, 11 rebounds and eight assists, tying Willis Reed 's franchise record with his 11th straight double-double to begin a season. Cleveland kept opening leads throughout the second half that New York would either nearly or entirely erase, only to quickly surge ahead again. The Cavs went ahead 95-85 with 8:25 remaining, but the Knicks responded with a 14-4 run to tie it. With the Cavs ahead by one, Evan Mobley scored before Jarrett Allen got the next four points, including a ferocious dunk to make it 110-103. Allen had 11 points and 14 rebounds for the Cavs, who had lost two in a row, including at home to the Knicks on Saturday. Harden was 4 for 4 in the second quarter, with three 3-pointers, for 13 points as the Cavaliers took a 59-53 lead at the half. Up next Cavaliers: Visit Miami on Friday night. Knicks: Visit Indiana on Friday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Celtics win 5th straight, overcoming 22-point deficit to beat Raptors 98-93
text: TORONTO -- — Jayson Tatum made the tying and go-ahead free throws with 25.2 seconds remaining and the Boston Celtics overcame a 22-point deficit to beat the Toronto Raptors 98-93 on Wednesday night, extending their winning streak to five. Tatum scored 24 points, Derrick White had 19 and Payton Pritchard added 14. Neemias Queta had 11 points and 13 rebounds as the Celtics improved to 4-0 against Atlantic Division opponents. Boston’s Paul George sat out because of an illness a night after he scored 36 points in a winning return to Philadelphia. Tatum shot 6 for 21 and finished 2 for 11 from 3-point range. He was 10 for 12 at the free throw line. Toronto’s Ja’Kobe Walter scored 17 points and rookie Allen Graves added a career-high 13, but the Raptors fell below .500 for the first time at 5-6. Raptors forward Kawhi Leonard (left knee) missed his ninth straight game but is “progressing well” with individual conditioning, coach Darko Rajakovic said before the game. On Tuesday, the Raptors said they'd update Leonard’s status in a week. Scottie Barnes (left groin) missed his third straight game but Immanuel Quickley returned after missing the past two because of a sore right hamstring. Collin Murray-Boyles started for the fourth time after sitting out Monday’s loss to Memphis because of illness. Walter scored all 12 of his points from long-range as the Raptors tied a franchise record for 3-pointers in a quarter by shooting 10 for 18 from distance in the first. Toronto shot 6 for 25 from distance the rest of the way. The Raptors led 59-37 after Jamal Shead’s free throw with 5:24 remaining in the second, but the Celtics answered with 16 straight points. Tatum scored the first 10 by himself as Boston cut the deficit to 61-54 at halftime. Up next Celtics: Host Dallas on Sunday. Raptors: At Philadelphia on Thursday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Wembanyama, Harper lead Spurs to 10th straight win, 124-119 over Bulls
text: CHICAGO -- — Victor Wembanyama scored 32 points, Dylan Harper had 18 points, 10 assists and four steals and the San Antonio Spurs won their 10th straight game, overcoming a 22-point deficit to beat the Chicago Bulls 124-119 on Wednesday night. The Bulls have lost eight in a row to fall to 1-9. They are 0-4 at home. Wembanyana also had nine rebounds and five blocks two days after his 40-point outburst in a win over the Phoenix Suns as the Spurs closed out a 4-0 trip. DeAaron Fox added 17 points and nine assists. Jalen Smith tied his career high with 23 points for the Bulls, and Nic Claxton had 17 off the bench. Bulls first-round pick Caleb Wilson scored 15 points in 15 minutes before leaving with a right hand injury in the third quarter. Wilson’s college season was cut short last winter by a pair of hand injuries. The Bulls led 64-42 midway through the second quarter, their biggest lead of the season, thanks to a 10-for-12 start from 3-point range. Chicago scored 41 points in the first quarter and shot 66% in the first half. The Spurs opened the third quarter with an 18-3 run to wipe out the Bulls' lead, enabled by five Chicago turnovers, then took control with an 11-2 run in the fourth quarter. Norman Powell , the Bulls' second-leading scorer, missed his second straight game with back spasms. Spurs guard Devin Vassell sat out his second in a row because of adductor tightness. Up next Spur: Host Golden State on Friday night. Bulls: Host Atlanta on Friday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Jamal Murray, Nikola Jokic lead Nuggets to 123-118 win over Grizzlies
text: MEMPHIS, Tenn. -- — Jamal Murray scored 17 of his 30 points in the fourth quarter, Nikola Jokic added 27 points, 11 rebounds and eight assists, and the Denver Nuggets held off the Memphis Grizzlies 123-118 on Wednesday night. Cameron Johnson finished with 23 points for the Nuggets, including a 3-pointer off a pass from Jokic with 1:01 left that put Denver ahead 120-113. Murray also had eight assists. Memphis rookie Cameron Boozer missed a 3-pointer that would have tied it with 6.9 seconds remaining. Ty Jerome scored 22 points — 11 in the fourth quarter — and Jaylen Wells also had 22 for the Grizzlies, who have lost four of five after winning their first six games. Memphis fell to 2-4 at home. Denver has won five of seven. The Nuggets never trailed and led by 18 points early in the second quarter, but the Grizzlies kept it close throughout the fourth. A basket by Jerome with 2:42 left got Memphis within 115-113, but Johnson scored the next five points. Cedric Coward had 15 points and 11 rebounds for Memphis, and Cam Spencer also scored 15. Boozer had 13 points and 11 rebounds. Up next Nuggets: At New Orleans on Saturday night. Grizzlies: At New Orleans on Friday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Doncic, Mamukelashvili and Reaves lead Lakers past Bucks 123-112 for 7th straight win
text: MILWAUKEE -- — Luka Doncic scored 32 points, Sandro Mamukelashvili added 23 and Austin Reaves 18 as the Los Angeles Lakers extended their winning streak to seven games with a 123-112 win over the Milwaukee Bucks on Wednesday night. Mamukelashvili, a second-round draft pick of the Bucks in 2021, matched a season-high for points set on Monday at Atlanta, and Reaves returned to action after missing Monday’s game due to illness. Walker Kessler had 10 points and 11 rebounds, and Collin Sexton chipped in with 10 points for Los Angeles, which improved to a league-best 11-2. Milwaukee’s season-scoring leader, Tyler Herro , who missed his first game of the season on Tuesday night because of a bruised right knee, returned with 25 points and seven assists. Jaime Jaquez Jr . scored a season-high 23 points for the Bucks, who lost their eighth straight and fell to 1-11. The Bucks jumped out to a 7-2 lead, but the Lakers quickly responded with a 9-0 run to pull ahead. Los Angeles’ lead grew to as many as nine before Milwaukee battled back within 30-28 after one quarter. Doncic had 16 points. The Bucks stayed close for most of the second quarter before a late push gave the Lakers a 61-50 lead at the half, despite Doncic being held to three points in the quarter. Mamukelashvili and Reaves each had 15 first-half points. The Lakers pulled away in the third, outscoring the Bucks 33-23 in the quarter to take a 94-73 lead. Herro and Ziaire Williams were whistled for technical fouls following a scuffle in the waning seconds of the period. Los Angeles scored 28 points off 19 Milwaukee turnovers. Up next Lakers: At Phoenix on Sunday. Bucks: Visit Orlando on Friday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Egor Demin scores 22 in his return as the Nets rout the Pelicans 145-111
text: NEW ORLEANS -- — Egor Demin returned from a six-game injury absence to score 22 points, Michael Porter Jr . also scored 22, and the Brooklyn Nets beat New Orleans 145-111 on Wednesday night, handing the Pelicans their fourth consecutive loss. Julius Randle had 17 while Noah Clowney and Moritz Wagner added 16 each for the Nets, who had eight players score in double-digits. Zion Williamson had 29 for the Pelicans, who have given up 138 points or more in three straight games, and have lost their last two by more than 30. The Pelicans lost by a franchise-record 51 points, 138-87, to Golden State on Sunday night. Saddiq Bey had 15 for New Orleans. The Nets shot 57% from the field in the game and finished 20 for 41 from 3-point range with nine different players hitting at least one, led by Porter and Demin with four each. Brooklyn led 83-66 at halftime. It was the Nets' most points in a first half since scoring 91 on Dec. 21, 2022 against Golden State. It was the third most in a first half in franchise history. The team record for points in a regulation game is 150. The Nets extended their lead to 124-84 during the fourth quarter, fueled by a 17-1 scoring run. The most points allowed by the Pelicans in a half is 87 to the Lakers in February 2024. Demin was back in the lineup after missing six games with a bone bruise in his leg. Pelicans wing Trey Murphy III missed his second straight game with knee soreness (bilateral patellar tendinopathy). Pelicans rookie Jaron Pierre Jr ., a second-round draft pick out of SMU and a New Orleans native, scored his first NBA basket. Up next Nets: Visit Memphis on Saturday night to conclude a four-game road trip. Pelicans: Host Memphis on Friday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Franz Wagner scores 38, helps Magic send Jazz to their 10th straight loss
text: SALT LAKE CITY -- — Franz Wagner matched a career high with 38 points and had eight rebounds to lead the Orlando Magic to a 123-108 victory over Utah on Wednesday night, the 10th straight loss for the Jazz. Desmond Bane had 25 points while Anthony Black chipped in 22 points and eight assists to help the Magic earn their second straight win and close out a four-game road trip with a 2-2 record. Orlando outscored the Jazz 14-3 in fast-break points and 40-28 in the paint. Darryn Peterson led Utah with 22 points and Brice Sensabaugh added 19. Ace Bailey had 18 points and a season-high four blocks for the Jazz who have not held an opponent under 110 points this season. After the Jazz took a 96-95 lead on Sensabaugh's 3-pointer, Orlando countered with an 18-3 run to go in front for good. Wagner scored two baskets, hit two free throws, and assisted on a 3-pointer by Bane to put the Magic up 113-99 with 3:39 remaining. Utah rarely attacked the basket early in the first half. Of the team's 28 field-goal attempts, 24 came from the perimeter. The Jazz took a 40-34 lead on back-to-back 3s from Sensabaugh and Keyonte George . Utah’s limited presence around the rim helped Orlando rally before halftime and take a 66-59 lead into the locker room. Wagner made four baskets and scored 13 points during the second quarter to help the Magic to surge in front. The Jazz scored baskets on six of their first seven possessions after halftime and took a 74-71 lead on Jaxson Hayes’ three-point play. Up Next Magic host Milwaukee on Friday night. Jazz at Houston on Friday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Rockets beat Warriors 115-108 to end Golden State’s 8-game winning streak after Curry's early exit
text: HOUSTON -- — Kevin Durant scored 20 points, Alperen Sengun and Amen Thompson added 19 and the Houston Rockets snapped Golden State’s eight-game winning streak with a 115-108 victory on Wednesday night. The Warriors played most of the game without Stephen Curry after the superstar left in the first quarter with right abdominal soreness and didn’t return. Golden State's longest winning streak since 2022 ended on a night they were held well below their season average of 120.4 points a game. Curry, who entered Wednesday ranked second in the NBA by averaging 30.6 points a game, had just three points before exiting. With Curry out, the Warriors were led by rookie Yaxel Lendeborg , who had 25 points and 10 rebounds. Brandin Podziemski added 22 points. The Rockets led by nine points early in the fourth quarter before the Warriors got 3-pointers from Georges Niang and De’Anthony Melton to cut the lead to 88-85 with about 10 minutes remaining. But Houston scored the next eight points, with an alley-oop dunk by Thompson before consecutive 3-pointers from Reed Sheppard to make it 96-85 with under nine minutes to go. The Warriors used a 6-0 run, with a four-point play by Podziemski, to get within 5. But, back-to-back 3s from Sheppard and Fred VanVleet left Houston up 102-91 midway through the quarter. Houston’s Marcus Smart was ejected late in the third quarter for punching Golden State’s Charles Bassey . It was unclear what started the altercation between the two, but Smart threw a punch that appeared to lightly strike Bassey’s nose. Smart was immediately pushed away by two other Warriors and an official grabbed Bassey around the waist and pulled him away. Smart didn’t wait for the officials to eject him, heading straight to the locker room after he was pulled away. The play was reviewed and he was issued a Flagrant 2 foul and ejected before play resumed. Up next Warriors: Visit San Antonio on Friday night as they continue a five-game road trip. Rockets: Host Utah on Friday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Trail Blazers sweep the Thunder with a 118-108 win
text: PORTLAND, Ore. -- — Deni Avdija had 28 points, Damian Lillard scored 18 points, and the Portland Trail Blazers completed a two-game sweep of the Oklahoma City Thunder with a 118-108 win on Wednesday night. Oklahoma City’s Shai Gilgeous-Alexander led all scorers with 31 points, including 23 in the second half, as the Thunder coughed up a fourth-quarter lead. Isaiah Hartenstein had 20 points and 11 rebounds. Portland center Donovan Clingan had 12 rebounds and 3 blocks, and Jrue Holiday pitched in 19 points off the bench. Oklahoma City trailed by 12 in the third quarter, but a 3-pointer by Nique Clifford tied the game at 88 with 11:11 left. A loose ball led to a layup by Kenrich Williams to give the Thunder their first lead since the first half and forcing a Blazers timeout with 10:41 left. Portland’s stars rallied the Blazers, with Avdija and Lillard scoring 20 of their 30 fourth-quarter points. Lillard’s 3-pointer with 6:17 left cut the lead to 94-93. After free throws by Gilgeous-Alexander and a putback by Robert Williams III , Portland took the lead back 99-98 on free throws by Avdija with 5:24 left. A floater by Lillard made it 108-100 with 2 minutes left. Free throws by Gilgeous-Alexander made it 108-102, only for Lillard to answer with a driving layup to make it 110-102. Jared McCain 's 3-pointer with 1:19 left pulled OKC within 110-105. But Lillard’s free throws made it 112-105 with a minute left. After trailing by as many as nine, Portland closed the 1st half on a 15-4 run. After technical foul on OKC coach Mark Daigenault made it 51-45, Holiday hit a 3-pointer with 1:13 left to make it 54-45. Up next Oklahoma City: Visits the L.A. Clippers on Friday night. Portland: Visits Sacramento on Friday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here
